title: When work is a pleasure
title_zh: 三百六十行，行行出状元。
theme: work, labor and leisure, pride in craftsmanship, attitude toward work

section_a.title: Will you be a worker or a laborer?
paragraphs: To be truly happy, a person must feel both free and important. People are never happy if they feel compelled to do work they do not enjoy, or if what they do enjoy is ignored as having no value or importance. In a society where slavery in the strict sense has been abolished, the social indications around work, the value of work, and the salary, have degraded many laborers into modern slaves – “wage slaves”.

People are considered laborers if their jobs have an adverse effect on them, yet they feel compelled to continue working by the necessity of conforming to societal expectations and earning the revenue to support themselves and their families. The polar opposite of labor is play. When we play a game, we enjoy what we are doing, but it is a purely private pastime; society does not care when or whether we play.

Between labor and play stands work. People are labeled as workers if their personal interests coincide with the jobs society pays them to do; what is necessary labor from the point of view of society is voluntary play from the individual's personal point of view. Whether a job is to be designated as labor or work depends, not on the job itself, but on the tastes of the individual who undertakes it. The difference does not, for example, correlate with the difference between a manual and mental job or between jobs with low or high income; a gardener covered in dirt in a greenhouse may be a worker while a well-dressed city mayor may prove to be an unhappy laborer!

Whether people are workers or laborers can be seen from their attitude toward leisure. To workers, leisure means simply the hours they need to relax and rest in order to work efficiently. Workers are therefore more likely to dedicate more time to working, taking too little leisure rather than too much. To laborers, on the other hand, leisure means autonomy from compulsion, so it is natural for them to imagine that the fewer hours they have to spend laboring, and the more hours they have free for play, the better.

Besides the hours spent in leisure, workers and laborers differ in the amount of personal satisfaction they derive from their jobs. Workers who enjoy their jobs will be happier, less stressed, and generally more satisfied with their lives. They will also work with more diligence and precision because they have fostered a sense of personal pride in their jobs. On the other hand, laborers, whose sole incentive is earning their livelihood, feel that the time they spend on the daily grind is wasted and doesn't contribute to their happiness. Instead of valuing all 24 hours of their day as enjoyable and productive hours, they gauge only the time spent in leisure and play as meaningful. Laborers are commonplace in society, but still many people are in the lucky position of being workers.

In recent decades, technological innovation and the division of labor have caused major economic changes by eliminating the need for special strengths or skills in many fields and have turned many paid occupations with enjoyable work into boring labor. Increasing productivity with automated machines, such as robots, has reduced the number of necessary laboring hours. It is possible to imagine an upcoming society in which the majority of the population will have almost as much leisure time as in earlier times was enjoyed by the medieval aristocracy. The medieval aristocrats had an abundance of leisure time but often wasted it in trivial pursuit of games and fashion. Likewise, modern day laborers with too much leisure time may find it difficult to refrain from the addictive and trivial pursuits of celebrity gossip, extravagant fashion, and excessive video games and TV – similar bad habits that waste valuable time.

However, it's not necessary to take such a toxic attitude toward such a positive thing as leisure time. In fact, in many countries, people now use their leisure time to improve their minds and their working conditions to create a happier, more contented life. Lifelong learning can make the difference between being bored, unhappy laborers and workers who find meaning and joy in their employment and lives. “Continuing education” or “experiential learning” can offer an array of classes from pleasant diversions such as sports, art, or music, to leadership development or advanced accounting skills, to name but a few.

All in all, people's attitude toward their work determines everything. Whatever the job, people who enjoy their work find time passes quickly. They hurl their passion into their work, be it physical like the work of a smith, or more mental like that of a scientist or an artist. Even purely mental work can suffice as an outlet, as aptly expressed by the phrase “sinking one's teeth into a problem”.

Eventually, everyone has to find a job and earn a living. Laborers are slaving away at a job they don't enjoy for a monetary reward, waiting all day until they go home and play. But while laborers are counting down the hours, workers are energized and focused, taking optimum pleasure in the task at hand. By choosing a job that is both useful to society and personally fulfilling, workers maintain a simultaneous sense of purpose and enthusiasm that improves their whole lives. So in the end, whatever job you choose, you must contend with this essential question: Will you be a laborer or a worker?

section_b.title: The joy of a prideful tradition
paragraphs: I first met him in 1965, when I rushed into his little shop to have the heels of my shoes repaired. He greeted me with a cheerful smile and instant hospitality. “You're new in this neighborhood, aren't you?”
Indeed, I had moved into a house at the end of the street only the week before.
“This is a fine neighborhood,” he said. “You'll be happy here.”

I sat there with my shoes off, watching as he got ready to stitch up my shoes I'd entrusted to him. He looked sadly at the leather covering the heel. It was worn through because I had failed to have the shoes patched a month ago. I grew a little impatient, for I was rushing to meet a friend. “Please hurry,” I begged.

He looked at me over his spectacles. “Now, don't worry. I won't be long. This handicraft is my specialty and I want to do a good job.” He was silent a moment. “You see, I have a tradition to live up to.”
A tradition? In this modest little shop that was no different from so many other shoe-repair shops on the residential side streets of Washington? The thought seemed a bit absurd.

He must have sensed my bias, for he smiled with a gleam in his eyes as he went on. “Yes, I inherited a tradition. My father always told me, ‘Son, do the best job on every shoe that comes into the shop, and be proud of your fine work. If you work with dedication, you'll always have happiness and money.’”
As he handed me the finished shoes, he said, “These will last a long time. I've used good leather.”

I left in a hurry, but I had a warm and grateful feeling. On my way home I passed the little shop again. There he was, sitting amongst his tools, still working. He saw me, and he waved and smiled, as cordial as could be. That was the beginning of our friendship, a fellowship that came to mean more and more to me as time passed.

Thereafter, we waved to each other in a friendly greeting when I passed his shop every day. At first I went in only when I had repair work to be done. Then I found myself lingering in his store or dropping in every few days, just to chat with him for the joy he would impart.

He was a tall man, bent from long years of work. What little hair he had was gray; his face was deeply lined. And, I remember best his fine dark eyes, alive with his charitable, carefree, and humorous spirit.

He was the happiest man I've ever known. Often, as he stood in front of his door overseeing the street, working at a pair of shoes, he sang a beautiful melody in a high, clear voice. Neighbors nicknamed him “the singing cobbler”. The neighborhood children loved him. He'd periodically pause his work to referee arguments or give out candy. He had no patience for bullying and would insist the children play fair in front of his store.

One day, I came away from my house filled with fury because of a poor job some painters had done on my house. My friend waved to me as I walked by, so I went into his shop to vent my frustration. He let me speak angrily about the poor work and carelessness of present-day workmen. “They had no pride in their work,” I said. “They just wanted to collect money for doing nothing! The undutiful attitude these days is almost a sin.”

He consoled me, saying, “There's a lot of that kind around, but maybe we should not blame them too rashly. Maybe their parents had no pride in their work. That's hard on a child. It keeps a child from learning what's important.”
“What can be done about it?” I asked.

He pondered that for a minute before answering. Then he looked at me seriously. “There is only one way. Every man or woman who hasn't inherited a prideful tradition must start building one. In this country, each of us can make our own contribution to the fabric of society, and we must endeavor to make it a good one. No matter what sort of work a person does, if they give it their best each day, they're starting a tradition for their children to live up to. When a person amends their ways and learns to take pride in their work, a lifetime of happiness will ensue.”

I traveled for a few months on business, and shortly after my return, I walked down the street, looking forward to seeing my friend again. Yet when I arrived, I found the door closed. There was a little sign: “Call for shoes at shop next door.”
I went into the next shop, and what I heard pierced my heart. Yes, the old man had passed away. He was stricken with an infectious illness two weeks before and died two days later.

I went away with a wretched void in my heart. I would miss him, terribly. But he had left me something, an important piece of wisdom I will invariably remember: “If you have inherited a prideful tradition, you must carry it on; if you haven't, then start building one now.”

section_c.title: Glassware on fire
paragraphs: Xing Lanxiang was hired by a glassware factory in Beijing after graduating from school in 1962. Before that, she had never heard of the art, and even afterward never did she expect to be engaged in it for the rest of her life. Today, together with her two sons, Xing is the heir of a national intangible cultural heritage and is the only glassware artist who has received the title of master in China.

In line with tradition, Xing followed a teacher, Tian Wenyuan, and after three years' apprenticeship, she was already very good at the art thanks to her diligence and passion. She always chose to tackle complicated work and soon became a leading figure in the factory. When the factory established its technology department in 1970, she became a member and studied the technology and designed new glassware products together with her co-workers.

This profession brought Xing a lot of pride, particularly during the heyday of her factory in the 1970s and 1980s, when the factory received a lot of foreign visitors every year. Glassware making is an art form that requires a product to be finished very quickly. Generally, a product is completed within a dozen minutes, while complicated ones are done within half an hour or one hour. So this is a feat that was often observed by visitors. Foreign visitors tended to favor this kind of traditional task very much.

However, the hardship of learning and grasping this skill makes the preservation of the art a major challenge. Xing once had more than 100 apprentices, but only one of them still remains in the sector, and now she has only her two sons to pass the skill on to. “Of course I hope the art of making glassware can be handed down from one generation to another, as it is really beautiful and represents a high level of art,” Xing said.

Xing never misses any opportunity to spread glassware culture. Through various activities, Xing has made more people aware of the art. She once attended the Glass Innovation Design Contest in Hejian of China's Hebei Province, where she exchanged views with masters in the sector. This further strengthened her confidence in the art of making glassware.

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How can a person be truly happy according to the author?
options: By earning a high salary and gaining social status
By feeling both free and important
By avoiding all forms of labor and living a life of play
By following societal expectations and conforming to them
questions.explanation: 第 1 段首句指出：To be truly happy, a person must feel both free and important.（一个人要真正幸福，必须感到既自由又重要。）

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How is labor different from play?
options: Labor is paid by society, while play is never enjoyable.
Labor is done under compulsion, while play is a purely private pastime that society does not care about.
Labor requires physical strength, while play requires mental effort.
Labor is always boring, while play always requires special skills.
questions.explanation: 第 2 段说明：labor 是迫于社会期待与生计而做（compelled to continue working），而 play 是 a purely private pastime，社会并不关心我们何时玩、是否玩。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why does the author make a comparison between a gardener and a well-dressed city mayor?
options: To show that manual jobs are more valuable than mental jobs.
To prove that a gardener earns more money than a mayor.
To show that whether a job counts as labor or work depends on the individual's taste, not on income or on manual vs. mental work.
To suggest that city mayors are usually unhappy laborers.
questions.explanation: 第 3 段说 labor 与 work 的区别不与 manual/mental、收入高低相关（does not correlate with…），并以满身泥土的园丁和西装革履的市长为例说明取决于做事者自己的喜好。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What does leisure mean to workers and laborers respectively?
options: To workers, the hours they need to relax and rest in order to work efficiently; to laborers, autonomy from compulsion.
To workers, complete freedom from all work; to laborers, a chance to earn extra income.
To workers, a private pastime; to laborers, a chance to work more hours.
To workers, time for family; to laborers, time for games and fashion.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段：To workers, leisure means simply the hours they need to relax and rest in order to work efficiently；To laborers… leisure means autonomy from compulsion。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How do workers and laborers differ in the amount of personal satisfaction they derive from their jobs?
options: Workers gain more satisfaction because they take pride in their work, while laborers feel their daily grind is wasted time.
Laborers gain more satisfaction because they earn more money.
Workers are less satisfied because they have to work longer hours.
There is no difference; both groups value all 24 hours of the day.
questions.explanation: 第 5 段：workers 因 fostered a sense of personal pride 而更快乐、更少压力；laborers 则认为 the time they spend on the daily grind is wasted。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How do technological innovation and the division of labor change the nature of work?
options: They have made every job more creative and enjoyable.
They have eliminated the need for special strengths or skills and turned many enjoyable paid occupations into boring labor.
They have increased the number of laboring hours for most people.
They have given all workers the same leisure time as medieval aristocrats.
questions.explanation: 第 6 段：技术创新与分工 by eliminating the need for special strengths or skills… have turned many paid occupations with enjoyable work into boring labor。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What kind of attitude should people take toward leisure time?
options: They should waste it in the trivial pursuit of games and fashion.
They should use it to improve their minds and working conditions and create a happier, more contented life.
They should spend it working extra hours for more money.
They should ignore it and concentrate only on their jobs.
questions.explanation: 第 7 段：不必对闲暇持 toxic attitude，人们 now use their leisure time to improve their minds and their working conditions to create a happier, more contented life，如终身学习。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why does the author mention “sinking one's teeth into a problem” (Para. 8)?
options: To show that purely mental work can also serve as an outlet for one's passion.
To explain why mental work is harder than physical work.
To describe how scientists and artists relax after work.
To warn people against becoming too involved in their work.
questions.explanation: 第 8 段：Even purely mental work can suffice as an outlet, as aptly expressed by the phrase “sinking one's teeth into a problem”，即纯脑力工作同样可以成为热情的宣泄出口。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: He is measuring the depth of the hole to ______ how much climbing line we'll need to get us down and back up again.
questions.explanation: gauge 意为“（根据所掌握的信息）估计、判断”，与 measuring the depth 呼应；foster 培养、suffice 足够、contend 竞争/主张均不合。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: He ______ for the lead in the final round, but ultimately finished in second position.
questions.explanation: contend for the lead 意为“争夺领先位置”，contend for 是固定搭配；conform 遵从、foster 培养、correlate 关联均不能与 for the lead 搭配。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Smartphone conversations, which are fairly ______ on commuter trains, can be annoying to fellow commuters.
questions.explanation: commonplace 意为“常见的、屡见不鲜的”，修饰 on commuter trains 上普遍存在的现象；adverse 不利的、upcoming 即将来临的、voluntary 自愿的语义不符。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Ask your doctor whether a low-fat diet and a daily walk will ______ to lower your high blood pressure.
questions.explanation: suffice to do sth. 意为“足以做某事”，符合“低脂饮食加每天散步是否足以降压”的语境。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: According to the latest statistics, most of the company's ______ is generated through the sale of smartphones.
questions.explanation: revenue 意为“（公司或组织的）收入，收益”，与 is generated through the sale 搭配；diversion 消遣、autonomy 自主、precision 精确均不合。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: Scientists have learned more about the ______ effects that human activities have on the environment and climate.
questions.explanation: adverse effects 是固定搭配，意为“不利影响、负面影响”，与 human activities 对环境的作用相符。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: I learned a great deal from this guide, and I am feeling very confident about my chances of passing the ______ exam.
questions.explanation: upcoming 意为“即将发生的、即将来临的”，修饰即将到来的考试；adverse、extravagant、medieval 都无法修饰 exam 表示“即将到来的”。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: There are rumors going around that this program will be ______ in November or December and all the work will be stopped.
questions.explanation: abolish 意为“废除、废止（制度、计划等）”，与 all the work will be stopped 一致。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: This program has transformed the airport's security screening area into an art gallery and is a pleasant ______ for travelers.
questions.explanation: diversion 意为“消遣、娱乐（让人不觉无聊的活动）”，与前句 art gallery 呼应；revenue 收入、autonomy 自主、pursuit 追求均不合。

questions.heading: Words in use
questions.question: We hope that the new series of music festivals will ______ interest in the arts in general and increase the city's international reputation.
questions.explanation: foster interest 意为“培养、促进兴趣”，是常见搭配；abolish 废除、suffice 足够、gauge 估计均不能与 interest 搭配。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: In the last half-century, women have entered into law ______ in increasing numbers, especially in larger police agencies.
questions.explanation: law enforcement 意为“执法”，与 police agencies 呼应；recruitment 招聘、shipment 运输、resentment 怨恨均不合语境。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: It took me two days to get the furniture cleaned, packed, and ready for ______ to my new home.
questions.explanation: shipment 由动词 ship 加 -ment 构成，意为“运输、装运”，ready for shipment to my new home 表示“准备运往新家”。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The museum's management had placed a ban on selling more than one duplicate print from the collection to avoid ______.
questions.explanation: commercialism 指“商业主义、唯利是图”，与博物馆限制重复出售藏品以避趋利的行为一致。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Within a work of magical ______, the world is still grounded in the real world, but fantastical elements are considered normal.
questions.explanation: magical realism 是固定说法“魔幻现实主义”，后文的 real world 与 fantastical elements 正是其特点。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: This is a well-known online ______ fair connecting job-seekers with leading employers looking for skilled talent.
questions.explanation: recruitment fair 意为“招聘会”，与 job-seekers、employers looking for skilled talent 直接对应。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Roman ______ introduced extremes of wealth and poverty that sharpened the social and economic conflicts within the Roman state.
questions.explanation: imperialism（帝国主义、扩张主义）与“罗马对外扩张导致贫富两极分化、加剧社会冲突”的历史语境相符。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: What impressed us most was that he did this without ______ or complaint, and had a great work ethic.
questions.explanation: resentment 意为“怨恨、不满”，与 or complaint 并列，说明他毫无怨言、职业道德良好。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: The book examines the results of terror attacks and analyzes the responses to ______.
questions.explanation: 由 terror attacks 可知此处指“恐怖主义”，terrorism 由 terror 加 -ism 构成。

questions.heading: Word building
questions.question: Here are two ways to avoid ______: discovering the joy of generosity and satisfying your spiritual hunger.
questions.explanation: materialism 意为“物质主义、拜金主义”，与“慷慨助人、满足精神需求”这两种解药形成对照。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Surprisingly, the study revealed that the ______ that people are happy when they have a good salary isn't true.
questions.explanation: notion 意为“观念、想法”，the notion that… 引出“高薪即快乐”这一被研究否定的看法；motion 运动、carrier 承运人、barrier 障碍均不合。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: So, what should people do to keep their spirits up and, at the same time, ______ a sense of joy at work?
questions.explanation: foster a sense of joy 意为“培养工作中的快乐感”，且此处需动词原形与 keep 并列；其余三项为 -ing 形式，语法不符。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Happiness is a state of mind, ______ an attitude.
questions.explanation: reflecting an attitude 意为“体现一种态度”，现在分词作伴随状语，说明心态即态度的反映。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Staying happy at work is totally based on your motivation and a positive outlook toward your job, not on ______ rewards or material gain.
questions.explanation: monetary rewards 与 material gain 并列，意为“金钱报酬”；exhaustive 详尽的、indebted 负债的、bored 厌烦的均不合。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Always remembering the good aspects of the work and ______ from thinking about what makes you unhappy are important to happiness.
questions.explanation: refrain from doing sth. 意为“克制不做某事”，refraining from thinking about… 与 remembering the good aspects 并列作主语。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Negativity and ______ about bad things are easy; it is looking at the bright side that is the difficult part of a job.
questions.explanation: complaining about bad things 意为“抱怨糟糕的事”，与 Negativity 并列，和 looking at the bright side 形成对比。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Rather than looking for help and ______ from other people, challenge yourself and take charge of your own growth professionally.
questions.explanation: incentives 意为“激励、动力”，与 help 并列，指来自他人的帮助与激励；clusters 群、barriers 障碍、notions 观念均不合。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: Getting ______ with work is one of the primary factors that cause people to switch jobs.
questions.explanation: get bored with sth. 意为“对……感到厌倦”，符合“对工作厌倦是跳槽主因”之意。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: So find new challenges and deal with them by making ______ plans and following them.
questions.explanation: exhaustive 意为“详尽的、彻底的”，exhaustive plans 指周密的计划，与 following them 搭配合理。

questions.heading: Banked cloze
questions.question: It is a good idea to have help from your manager if you hit a(n) ______, but completely relying on someone for your career advancement is unwise.
questions.explanation: hit a barrier 意为“遇到障碍”，与“完全依赖他人不明智”的转折逻辑一致；carrier 承运人、cluster 群、motion 运动均不合。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The rapid rise in unemployment does ______ the increase in young people living at home, according to research.
questions.explanation: correlate with 意为“与……相关”，用于说明失业率上升与年轻人住在家里的增加之间存在关联。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: It was a moment of overwhelming excitement when Steve was given the first prize; Tiffany couldn't ______ hugging and kissing him.
questions.explanation: can't refrain from doing sth. 意为“忍不住做某事”，符合 Tiffany 激动得忍不住拥抱亲吻他的语境。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: I guarantee they will ______ to come and spend time with you because you have made them feel welcome.
questions.explanation: be counting down the days 意为“翘首以盼、数着日子等待”，后接 to come and spend time with you。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: She spent the next 10 years ______ to pay back the money they had borrowed from the bank.
questions.explanation: slave away 意为“拼命干、苦干”，与 spend the next 10 years doing 结构及“还债”语境相符。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: This is a rare opportunity and he just can't wait to ______ the interesting new project.
questions.explanation: sink one's teeth into sth. 意为“全身心投入、专注于某事”，与 can't wait to 连用表达迫不及待投入新项目。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The travel agency offers considerate care for its customers when they encounter unplanned circumstances or must ______ an unfamiliar environment.
questions.explanation: contend with 意为“（不得不）处理、对付（问题或困境）”，与 an unfamiliar environment 搭配。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: One teacher will be ______ the distance learning teacher for students who choose to start the school year that way.
questions.explanation: designate sb./sth. as 意为“指定、任命为”，此处为被动 be designated as the distance learning teacher。

questions.heading: Expressions in use
questions.question: The deepening cooperation between the two countries meets the development needs of both sides and ______ the will of the people of both sides.
questions.explanation: conform to 意为“符合、遵从”，conform to the will of the people 即“顺应两国人民的意愿”。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: The author went quickly into the shop to ______.
options: meet one of her old friends
questions.explanation: 第 1 段：I first met him in 1965, when I rushed into his little shop to have the heels of my shoes repaired. 即去修鞋跟。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why did the author become a little impatient?
options: She was in a hurry to meet a friend.
It took a long time to have her shoes repaired.
The shoe repairer was sad and did nothing about her torn shoes.
She couldn't put up with the shoe repairer's carelessness.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段末：I grew a little impatient, for I was rushing to meet a friend. “Please hurry,” I begged.

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: How did the author feel when the shoe repairer first mentioned that he had a tradition to live up to?
questions.explanation: 第 6 段作者心里反问：A tradition? In this modest little shop…? The thought seemed a bit absurd. 说明她当时将信将疑。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What is the tradition the shoe repairer's father handed down to him?
options: Treating all the clients with hospitality.
Finding pleasure in what a person does.
Being dedicated to work and feeling proud.
questions.explanation: 第 7 段引父亲的话：do the best job on every shoe… and be proud of your fine work. If you work with dedication…，即敬业并以自己的工作为荣。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: Why did the author drop into the shoe-repair shop very frequently?
options: The shoe repairer would bring her joy.
She wanted to have someone to chat with.
She could listen to the shoe repairer's songs.
questions.explanation: 第 10 段：I found myself lingering in his store or dropping in every few days, just to chat with him for the joy he would impart. 即为了他带来的快乐。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What do we know about the shoe repairer?
options: He earned more money than needed.
Children regarded him as a trustworthy man.
He often sang songs to the neighborhood children.
Neighbors often had their shoes repaired in his shop.
questions.explanation: 第 12 段：他边修鞋边唱歌，邻居称他“the singing cobbler”，街坊孩子喜爱他，他会停下活儿给孩子裁判争执、发糖果。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: The shoe repairer explained that the poor work the painters had done was owing to the painters' lack of ______.
questions.explanation: 第 14 段：Maybe their parents had no pride in their work. 第 16 段进一步说要 start building a prideful tradition，即缺少引以为傲的传统。

questions.heading: Reading comprehension
questions.question: What wisdom did the shoe repairer impart to the author?
options: It is important to be kind to people around you.
It is important to be happy with what you are doing.
It is important to be good at your own handicraft.
It is important to start, keep, and carry on a prideful tradition.
questions.explanation: 全文结尾点题：If you have inherited a prideful tradition, you must carry it on; if you haven't, then start building one now.

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Do you feel happy at work? Are you a happy worker or an ______?
questions.explanation: Text A 的核心对立是 happy workers 与 unhappy laborers，故与 a happy worker 对应的是 an unhappy laborer。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Let me introduce Valerie, who finds her work — cleaning the ladies' toilets — ______.
questions.explanation: Text A 中 find a job personally fulfilling 意为“在工作中获得个人满足”，此处名词形式为 personal fulfillment。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: My point: You can always find ______ at work regardless of what you do.
questions.explanation: optimum pleasure 出自 Text A：taking optimum pleasure in the task at hand，意为“在工作中获得最大的乐趣”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Many companies get it wrong when it comes to making employees ______.
questions.explanation: Text A 开篇 feel truly happy 意为“真正感到快乐”，此处作 make employees truly happy（使员工真正快乐）。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: They try to create a happy workplace through things like ______, free gym membership, or health care.
questions.explanation: monetary reward 出自 Text A“金钱报酬”，与免费健身房、医疗保险并列为公司常用的物质手段。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Working with the ______ of earning a living will not make people happy.
questions.explanation: sole incentive 出自 Text A：laborers, whose sole incentive is earning their livelihood，即“唯一动机是谋生”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Results create happiness when you achieve something, make a difference, and create value, which bring you ______.
questions.explanation: Text A 中 personal satisfaction 指“个人满足感”，与 achieve something, make a difference, create value 的结果对应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: It is the seemingly ______ that is a key source of happiness at work.
questions.explanation: trivial pursuit 出自 Text A：the addictive and trivial pursuits of celebrity gossip…，此处指看似琐碎的日常小事。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: There are many different ways of praising and recognizing ______, whether it is a congratulatory email, an announcement in a meeting, or a picture on a bulletin board.
questions.explanation: special strengths 出自 Text A：use your special strengths to resolve problems，指员工各自的“特长”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: It should be known that recognition is earned by your impressive performance at work rather than your ______.
questions.explanation: high income 出自 Text A：between jobs with low or high income，此处与 impressive performance 对照，指高收入。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: For some people, joy and work might seem like ______, but relationships can bring happiness to your work.
questions.explanation: polar opposites 出自 Text A：The polar opposite of labor is play，意为“完全对立的两件事”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: After a ______, you drink coffee or have a lunch with your colleagues.
questions.explanation: friendly greeting 出自 Text B：we waved to each other in a friendly greeting，即“友好的问候”。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: With a ______, you talk about your personal life and work with them happily to resolve problems.
questions.explanation: cheerful smile 出自 Text B：He greeted me with a cheerful smile，即“愉快的微笑”，与 happily 呼应。

questions.heading: Collocation
questions.question: Every day you have countless opportunities to shape and reshape your co-worker relationships, and don't let them have an ______ on your work experience.
questions.explanation: adverse effect 出自 Text A：have an adverse effect on them，意为“对……产生不利影响”。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: When did Xing Lanxiang start working at the glassware factory?
options: In 1970, when the technology department opened
In the 1980s, when the factory was at its peak
In 1950, before she entered a technical school
questions.explanation: 第1段：邢兰香1962年毕业后被北京一家玻璃器皿厂录用，此前她从未听说过这门手艺。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: How long was Xing's apprenticeship under Tian Wenyuan?
questions.explanation: 第2段：按传统她拜田文元为师，三年学徒期满后已非常熟练。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: How long does a complicated piece of glassware usually take to finish?
options: Half an hour to one hour
questions.explanation: 第3段：一般作品十几分钟完成，复杂作品需半小时到一小时，因此常引来外宾围观。

questions.heading: Stories of China
questions.question: What makes it hard to preserve the art of glassware making?
options: Few people can master and pass on the skill
The factory no longer receives foreign visitors
The raw materials are becoming too expensive
The art is no longer protected by the state
questions.explanation: 第4段：学艺难度大，邢兰香曾有100多名徒弟，如今只剩一人留在行业里，只能把技艺传给两个儿子。

translation.zh: 近年来，社会的发展和就业形势的变化对大学生提出了更高的要求。
translation.en_reference: In recent years, social development and changes in the employment situation have placed higher demands on college students.

translation.zh: 越来越多的大学生不再局限于学习书本知识，而是利用业余时间积极投身于社会实践活动。
translation.en_reference: More and more college students no longer confine themselves to book knowledge; instead, they devote their spare time to social practice activities.

translation.zh: 通过社会实践活动，他们可以提高分析问题和解决问题的能力，更深入地了解社会，增强社会责任感。
translation.en_reference: Through social practice activities, they can improve their ability to analyze and solve problems, gain a deeper understanding of society, and strengthen their sense of social responsibility.

translation.zh: 同时，参加社会实践活动还可以帮助他们认识到自身的不足，明确未来努力的方向。
translation.en_reference: At the same time, participating in social practice activities can also help them recognize their own shortcomings and clarify the direction of their future efforts.

writing.prompt: Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics, using the point-by-point pattern of comparison and contrast developed in Text A. Topic: Continuing to study or going to work. One topic has an outline that you can follow.
outline: Introduction: state the thesis that deciding whether to continue your studies or go to work will have different and profound impacts on your future life and career.
Point 1: Your decision will influence the way you spend your time at college — continuing to study means more classes and campus life, while going to work replaces study time with office duties.
Point 2: Your decision has financial implications — continuing to study involves tuition costs and delayed earnings, whereas going to work brings in a salary at once.
Point 3: Your decision will have a great impact on your future job opportunities; conclude that you should be clear about these possible impacts before making the final decision.

notes: Text A：原 OCR 把第 7、8 段合并为一段（并夹入乱码“&”），已按 page_103 拆为两段，最终 9 段。
Text B：原 OCR 把第 4/5 段、第 10/11 段、第 14/15 段分别合并，第 15 段只剩乱码“1S … se Eng”；已按 page_114–page_115 还原为 19 段。
Section C：原文为双栏 OCR，两栏交错串行（如“Design Contest in Hejian…”插入段落中间），已按 page_122–page_123 重排为 5 段；标题由“Classware on firs”还原为 Glassware on fire。
Section C 正文中的中文注释（非物质文化遗产／学徒期／全盛时期）按规格从英文正文中删除，未改动英文。
words 依 New words 页（page_104–page_107、page_116–page_118）校对：修正 toxic、bullying、charitable 等拼写，补全 void 的词义（page_118），pos 统一为教材缩写并去掉音标。
New words 中原 OCR 漏收 contend、optimum（Text A）、periodically（Text B），已依 page_105–page_106、page_117 补入。
Phrases and expressions（to name but a few、sink one's teeth into sth.、slave away、be counting down the days、at hand、contend with sth.、stitch sth. up、live up to sth. 等）未导出到 words，如需短语词条可另行补充。
跳过 Critical thinking / Work in pairs 讨论题共 6 题（Text A 3 题、Text B 3 题）；Section A Pre-reading activities 1–2（评分表与配对讨论）无法客观判分，未收录。
Banked cloze（page_109）教材未给答案，按上下文与排除法确定：notion / foster / reflecting / monetary / refraining / complaining / incentives / bored / exhaustive / barrier。

Section B Collocation（page_120–page_121）第 2 空依 Text A“personally fulfilling”取名词形式 personal fulfillment，第 10 空首字母提示为 h… i…，取 high income。
